title: Hosts and Hostesses, Restaurant, Lounge, and Coffee Shop
description: Welcome patrons, seat them at tables or in lounge, and help ensure quality of facilities and service.

clusters.label: Communicating with People Outside the Organization

tasks.text: Provide guests with menus.
Answer telephone calls and respond to inquiries or transfer calls.
Direct patrons to coatrooms and waiting areas, such as lounges.
Inform patrons of establishment specialties and features.
Greet guests and seat them at tables or in waiting areas.
Assign patrons to tables suitable for their needs and according to rotation so that servers receive an appropriate number of seatings.
Inspect dining and serving areas to ensure cleanliness and proper setup.
Inspect restrooms for cleanliness and availability of supplies, and clean restrooms when necessary.
Assist other restaurant workers by serving food and beverages, or by bussing tables.
Take and prepare to-go orders.
Supervise and coordinate activities of dining room staff to ensure that patrons receive prompt and courteous service.
Perform marketing and advertising services.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Maintain contact with kitchen staff, management, serving staff, and customers to ensure that dining details are handled properly and customers' concerns are addressed.

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Speak with patrons to ensure satisfaction with food and service, to respond to complaints, or to make conversation.
Operate cash registers to accept payments for food and beverages.
Prepare cash receipts after establishments close, and make bank deposits.
Receive and record patrons' dining reservations.
Order or requisition supplies and equipment for tables and serving stations.
Hire, train, and supervise food and beverage service staff.
Confer with other staff to help plan establishments' menus.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Facebook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Avenista Table Reservations, GuestBridge Reserve, OpenTable, Reservation software.

skills.name: Point of sale POS software
skills.def: Software to enable billing and purchase of goods or services at retail markets or shops. May provide sales reports. Examples: Hospitality Control Solutions Aloha Point-of-Sale.
